questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Macrophages are professional APCs. They phagocytose antigen and present it on MHC class II to CD4+ T cells.

options.label: B
options.explanation: T cells recognise antigen that other cells present. They are not professional APCs.

options.label: C
options.explanation: B cells are professional APCs. They take up antigen through the B-cell receptor and present it on MHC II to helper T cells.

options.label: D
options.explanation: NK cells are innate killer lymphocytes. They kill cells that lack MHC I and do not present antigen.

questions.pearl: The 3 professional APCs: dendritic cells (the most potent), macrophages and B cells.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sunken eyes are one of the IMCI signs. Two of the signs together classify as some dehydration.

options.label: B
options.text: Skin pinch goes back very slowly
options.explanation: 'Very slowly' (more than 2 seconds) is a sign of severe dehydration. In some dehydration the skin pinch goes back slowly.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Drinking eagerly / thirsty is a sign of some dehydration. In severe dehydration the child drinks poorly or is unable to drink.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A lethargic or unconscious child falls under severe dehydration. In some dehydration the child is restless and irritable.

questions.pearl: Some dehydration = 2 of: restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, skin pinch goes back slowly. Treat with Plan B (ORS 75 ml/kg over 4 hours).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: A fine cobweb (pellicle) clot forms when TB CSF is left standing, because of its high protein (fibrinogen).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Opening pressure is raised, often because of basal exudates causing communicating hydrocephalus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Protein is markedly raised (often 1–5 g/L), and very high in spinal block.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Glucose is low (CSF:blood ratio below 0.5), as in bacterial meningitis.

questions.pearl: TB CSF: clear/cobweb, lymphocytes, ↑↑ protein, ↓ glucose, ADA raised. Viral CSF has normal glucose.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: It typically occurs in elderly, post-menopausal (osteoporotic) women after a fall on the outstretched hand. Young adults get high-energy distal radius fractures instead.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dorsal displacement of the distal fragment gives the classic dinner-fork deformity on lateral view.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The distal radius fragment is dorsally angulated/tilted, radially deviated and impacted, within 2.5 cm of the wrist.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sudeck's atrophy (complex regional pain syndrome) is a recognised late complication of Colles' fracture.

questions.pearl: Colles complications: malunion (most common), stiffness, Sudeck's atrophy, carpal tunnel syndrome, delayed rupture of extensor pollicis longus.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cervical dilatation is plotted against time with the alert and action lines. It is the core of the partograph.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fetal condition (FHR, liquor, moulding) is charted, usually every 30 minutes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Frequency and duration of contractions per 10 minutes are recorded.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Crossing the alert/action line shows prolonged labour early, which helps prevent obstructed labour.

questions.pearl: WHO partograph starts in the active phase (cervix 4 cm). Action line is 4 hours to the right of the alert line.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cirrhosis causes a transudate (low protein, SAAG ≥ 1.1 g/dL) from portal hypertension and hypoalbuminaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Classically a transudate (high SAAG). Protein may be mildly raised, but for exams count CCF as transudative.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Peritoneal carcinomatosis gives a protein-rich exudate, often blood-stained, with malignant cells.

options.label: D
options.explanation: TB peritonitis gives an exudate: high protein, lymphocytes and raised ADA.

questions.pearl: Exudate (protein > 25 g/L): malignancy, TB, pancreatitis. Transudate: cirrhosis, CCF, nephrotic syndrome. SAAG ≥ 1.1 g/dL means portal hypertension.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cholesteatoma can erode the fallopian canal and cause lower motor neuron facial palsy (an intratemporal complication).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Attico-antral (unsafe) CSOM is associated with cholesteatoma, which erodes bone.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Toxins spreading through the round window, or labyrinthitis/fistula, can cause SNHL on top of the conductive loss.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lateral (sigmoid) sinus thrombosis is a classic intracranial complication of unsafe CSOM.

questions.pearl: Intracranial complications of CSOM: meningitis (most common), brain abscess (temporal lobe / cerebellum), lateral sinus thrombosis, extradural abscess.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Isoniazid is a recognised (less common) cause of gynaecomastia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Digoxin has an oestrogen-like structure and can cause gynaecomastia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Spironolactone is the classic cause: it blocks androgen receptors and testosterone synthesis. Eplerenone avoids it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beta-blockers are not associated with gynaecomastia.

questions.pearl: Mnemonic 'DISCO': Digoxin, Isoniazid, Spironolactone, Cimetidine, Oestrogens. Add ketoconazole, GnRH analogues and finasteride.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Excess TSH drives the thyroid, so T3 rises.

options.label: B
options.explanation: T4 also rises because of TSH stimulation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The cause is a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma, so TSH is high or inappropriately normal along with high T3/T4.

options.label: D
options.text: Pathology lies in the thyroid gland
options.explanation: The pathology is in the pituitary. Disease of the thyroid gland itself (Graves', toxic nodule) is primary hyperthyroidism, with suppressed TSH.

questions.pearl: Primary hyperthyroidism: ↑T3/T4, ↓TSH. Secondary: ↑T3/T4 with ↑ or normal TSH.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Apoptosis is programmed cell death. Once it starts, the cell is lost, so it is an end point of irreversible injury.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Necrosis is the classic result of irreversible injury: membrane damage, nuclear changes (pyknosis, karyorrhexis, karyolysis) and inflammation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Metaplasia is a reversible adaptation in which one adult cell type is replaced by another (e.g. Barrett's oesophagus).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hyperplasia is a reversible adaptation: an increase in cell number.

questions.pearl: Hallmarks of irreversibility: inability to reverse mitochondrial dysfunction and severe membrane damage. Reversible signs: cell swelling and fatty change.
